input.summary: ADV-8 ad spend (toys; DE 61%, FR 39%) was 511.16 EUR against 13.25 EUR expected over the 6h window (+497.91). The baseline expects about 0 spend from 19:00 to 23:00. Decomposition: higher click volume adds +372.05 EUR (74.8%). All of the click increase comes from more impressions, and CTR is slightly negative. A higher cost per click adds +125.33 EUR (25.2%). CPC sits at a fixed ~2.635 EUR against 0.613 expected, which looks like a set bid level. The surge started at or before 2026-11-25T19:00, the start of the evidence window. The only other toys advertiser, ADV-5, is flat (-0.5 EUR). That rules out Black Friday seasonality and any toys-wide cause. The unplanned search-ranker (DE) and search-ui (FR) releases at 2026-11-27T00:00 came after most of the excess spend, so they are decoys. Data freshness is ok. The Skeptic ruled out innocence: no plan or seasonal pattern explains the spike. The leading explanation is an ADV-8-specific campaign, budget, bid or daypart change. It stays unconfirmed because the only evidence is the metrics themselves. No change-log entry or seller-side fact backs it, and no specialists were available.

input.summary: Web first_party_margin at 2026-11-27T03:00Z was 245.91 against 843.13 expected (delta -597.22, z -13.65), and freshness was ok (ref-1, ref-2). The drop is concentrated in the web search channel: search margin was 8.85 against 667.96 expected (delta -659.11, 109% of the entry delta), partly offset by the 'other' channel at +119.78 (ref-6). Within DE, search fell -330.34 (ref-9). FR web and the feed channel returned no rows (actual null) even though FR freshness was reported ok (ref-4, ref-5). Web fell -71.1% while iOS fell -20.5% and was not anomalous (z -1.13) (ref-10), so the problem looks specific to web. Two unplanned releases happened at 2026-11-27T00:00Z: search-ranker v7.2 in DE and search-ui v3.0 in FR (ref-8). They line up with the search and country pattern, but web margin first changed at 2026-11-26T23:00Z, one hour earlier. Web search margin first changed even earlier, at 13:00Z (ref-11, ref-12). So the timing does not support either release as the trigger. open_questions: What web-only change happened at or just before 2026-11-27T00:00? Check web feature flags, config pushes and CDN changes, which are not in the change log.
Did the checkout-web release of 2026-11-26T10:00 contain a delayed or flagged feature that switched on at midnight?
What caused the web client_error_rate anomaly from 2026-11-26T04:00, and did it touch the checkout component even though errors are normal now?
Are web checkout-page load or step-level funnel events (cart view → checkout start) failing silently, without showing up as client errors?
suggested_actions: Page the checkout-web owners: check feature flags and config changes on web around 2026-11-27T00:00, and roll back any found.
If no other web change turns up, prepare to roll back the 2026-11-26T10:00 checkout-web release.
Run a synthetic web checkout in DE and FR to reproduce the cart→checkout failure.
Watch the web cart_to_checkout_rate against iOS as a control each hour until it recovers.
input.summary: Web cart_to_checkout_rate at 2026-11-27T01:00 was 0.6667 against an expected 0.8333 (delta -0.1667, z=-10). The data is complete (freshness ok). The drop affects web only: iOS is +0.7% and Android is up. It hits both web countries, DE (73% of the delta) and FR (27%). Almost all of it is a lower conversion rate within each country, not a change in the country mix (rate -0.164, mix -0.006). Web first went anomalous at 2026-11-27T00:00. The two unplanned search releases that hour (DE search-ranker v7.2, FR search-ui v3.0) are ruled out, because they targeted countries rather than platforms, yet iOS in the same countries is flat. Client errors are also ruled out: they are normal in the window (z=-0.19). The 14h-earlier checkout-web routine release is the only web-specific change, but it has no planned effect and nothing moved for 14h after it. The underlying cause is not established. The Skeptic found the drop is not explained by plans or seasonality.

content.text: {"title":"DE search-ranker v7.2 release drives -45.8% drop in search first-party margin","summary":"Verdict: CONFIRMED. Search-channel first-party margin at 2026-11-27T01:00 was 2139.78 EUR vs 3951.305 expected (delta -1811.5, -45.8%, z -22.9), with an estimated impact of about 1878 EUR/hour. Data was complete and fresh. The supported root cause is the unplanned search-ranker v7.2 release scoped to DE, deployed 2026-11-27T00:00. That is exactly when DE search margin first changed. DE accounts for 95% of the delta (-1698.6, -67.9%), while the FR control is normal (-5.8%, z -0.2). The DE drop is cross-platform (iOS -86%, Android -68%, web -33%) and limited to search: in DE, feed (+149.76) and other channels (+319.18) rose. Two alternatives were refuted. The FR search-ui v3.0 release is ruled out because FR is not anomalous (delta -82.43). The Android routine release at 2026-11-26T22:00 is ruled out because the drop is cross-platform, iOS drops more, and the first change came two hours after that release. The skeptic check found no planned effect or seasonality that explains the drop. Uncertainty: the discovery agent was unavailable, so there is no trace-level confirmation of the ranker's behavior. Open questions: (1) which v7.2 ranking change reduced 1P margin, such as demoting 1P offers, boosting lower-margin items, or lowering search conversion; (2) whether the DE feed and other-channel gains are traffic displaced from search. Affected: search-ranker (DE), DE search users on iOS, Android and web, and first-party electronics and home categories. Suggested actions: roll back or feature-flag off v7.2 in DE and monitor recovery; have the search-ranker owners review the v7.2 diff for how 1P electronics and home listings are treated; require expected-effect plans and staged rollouts with margin guardrails for unplanned search-ranker releases."}

decisions.reason: Toys share of ad_revenue is 16.9% against 2.8% expected, up about 14 percentage points (z 292.6, complete data). This matches open incident inc_6053: same metric, same toys segment, root avg_cpc.
Same toys share shift in ad_spend: 16.9% against 2.8% expected. It is the ad_revenue counterpart of the same toys/ADV-8 CPC change, so it belongs with open incident inc_6053.

Android cart_rate is 4.70% against 6.42% expected, a 27% relative drop (z -13.4, 100% complete, about €703/h). A planned app-android release went out at 22:00. The open cart_rate incident covers only DE, not android, so this is opened as the most upstream signal of the cart and GMV drops.

Total GMV is €11,484 against €14,909 expected, down 23% (z -11.4, complete data, €3,426/h). This is likely a downstream result of the android cart_rate drop being investigated, so no duplicate investigation. Attach once that result is in; recheck next tick.

Web checkout_conversion is 0.789 against 0.661 expected, up 19% (z 9.7, complete data). This is the same web checkout funnel and segment as open incident inc_fd105 (cart_to_checkout_rate, platform=web).

Total carts are 100 against 142 expected, down 30% (z -9.4, complete data). This is likely a downstream symptom of the android cart_rate drop being investigated, so no duplicate investigation. Attach after that result; recheck next tick.
Android carts are 43 against 61.5 expected, down 30% (z -8.3, complete data). This is a direct downstream symptom of the android cart_rate drop being investigated. Attach after that result.

Total checkout_conversion is 0.72 against 0.62 expected, up 16% (z 8.1, complete data). This is plausibly a mix effect of the web rise (incident inc_fd105) and fewer android carts, so no separate investigation for now. Recheck next tick.
ADV-8 share of ad_revenue is 16.3% against 1.8% expected. Incident inc_6053's fingerprint names ADV-8 in toys with root avg_cpc, so this belongs there.
ADV-8 share of ad_spend is 16.3% against 1.8% expected. This is the same CPC-change incident as inc_6053.

At 03:00, the web client error rate was 0.31% against an expected 0%. The baseline has zero variance, so the z of about 3.06M is inflated. Estimated impact is €0/h and this is the first hour. Recheck next tick because client errors may feed the open web cart_to_checkout incident.
Search orders were 31 against 61.5 expected (-49.6%, z -24.8, €867/h) with complete data. The validated graph path cart_rate → carts → orders links this to the open DE cart_rate incident.
DE orders were 22 against 53 expected (-58.5%, z -20.9, €881/h) with complete data. This is the same DE segment, and the open DE cart_rate incident reaches orders through cart_rate → carts → orders.

Search GMV was €5,574 against €10,565 expected (-47.2%, z -16.3, about €4,991/h) with complete data. It follows from the search orders drop through gmv = orders × aov. The graph path cart_rate → carts → orders → gmv links it to the open DE cart_rate incident.

Web first-party margin was €245.91 against €843.13 expected (-70.8%, z -13.7, €619/h) with complete data. No open incident matches the web segment, and no graph path from an open incident root reaches it, so this is the highest-priority unexplained signal.
DE cart rate was 3.67% against 7.63% expected (-3.96 pp, -51.9% relative, z -11.7, €1,236/h) with complete data. The metric and segment exactly match the open DE cart_rate incident.

Total checkout conversion was 53.6% against 69.3% expected (-15.7 pp, -22.6% relative, z -11.3, €538/h). This is the second consecutive hour after last tick's watch. Instead of opening a duplicate, attach it to the open web cart_to_checkout incident: the validated formula checkout_conversion = cart_to_checkout_rate × checkout_to_payment_rate × payment_success_rate links them.

Total orders were 52 against 84.5 expected (-38.5%, z -11.0, €924/h). The DE orders shortfall of 31 explains nearly all of the 32.5-order gap. It is downstream of the open DE cart_rate incident through cart_rate → carts → orders.

The Android client error rate fell to 0% from an expected 0.26% (z -38.9) in the first hour, after the planned app-android release at 22:00. Zero errors could mean an improvement or broken error logging. Recheck next tick.
DE first-party margin was €773.91 against €1,702.25 expected (-54.5%, z -8.7, €963/h) with complete data. The metric family and DE segment match the open DE search first-party margin incident.
